cues.en: How much do you know about lines?
cues.zh: 你对排队了解多少？

cues.en: A line or a queue is an organized group of people, or in this case dots, waiting their turn for some thing.
cues.zh: 队列是一群有组织的人，或者在这里，是一群点，排队等着做某件事。

cues.en: The amount of time it takes to get from the start of the queue to the end of the queue is the wait time. In its simplest form, the wait time is affected by two factors, the service rate and the arrival rate. The service rate is the rate at which people get pulled from the queue to do the thing. The arrival rate is the rate at which people arrive to the queue.
cues.zh: 从队首到队尾所需的时间就是等待时间。最简单的情况下，等待时间受两个因素影响：服务速率和到达速率。服务速率是人被从队列中拉出来去做事的速度。到达速率是人到达队列的速度。

cues.en: Speed up the service and the wait time decreases.
cues.zh: 加快服务，等待时间就会减少。

cues.en: Increase the arrival rate and the wait time increases.
cues.zh: 提高到达率，等待时间就会增加。

cues.en: At its core, this is all a line is. How fast do people get in line and how fast do they get out? But in any real world scenario, queues become anything but simple, and there's no better showcase of this complexity than the Disney parks. Disney is world famous not only for their wait times, but for the bold strategies that they have implemented to cut them down. To truly understand this topic, it is not enough to simply learn the history. We must deep dive into the technicalities and psychology of queuing, and fully examine the many ways that Disney has tried to tackle the issue of lines.
cues.zh: 本质上，队列就是这么回事。人们排队有多快，离开有多快？但在任何现实场景中，队列都远不止这么简单，而迪士尼乐园就是这种复杂性的最佳展示。迪士尼闻名世界，不仅因为等待时间，还因为他们为缩短等待时间而实施的激进策略。要真正理解这个话题，仅仅了解历史是不够的。我们必须深入探讨排队的技​​术细节和心理学，并全面考察迪士尼为解决排队问题所尝试的多种方法。

cues.en: And unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: there is no fast pass for this explanation.
cues.zh: 这个解释没有快速通行证。

cues.en: So without further wait, let's take an excruciatingly
cues.zh: 所以不再等待，让我们来一次极其

cues.en: deep dive into everybody's least favorite aspect of theme parks.
cues.zh: 深入地探讨主题公园里大家最不喜欢的方面。

cues.en: Walt Disney World opened to the public with two resort hotels and one theme park, the Magic Kingdom. Within the first year of opening, Walt Disney World began to experience the problem that had long plagued Disneyland Park in Anaheim,
cues.zh: 华特迪士尼世界向公众开放，拥有两家度假酒店和一个主题乐园——神奇王国。在开业的第一年，华特迪士尼世界就开始遇到长期困扰阿纳海姆迪士尼乐园的问题，

cues.en: long waits for attractions.
cues.zh: 那就是游乐项目排队时间过长。

cues.en: Two of the most dreaded waits were for the 20,000
cues.zh: 最令人头疼的两个排队项目是“海底两万里”

cues.en: Under the Sea ride and the Country Bear Jamboree show. The wait for 20,000
cues.zh: （20,000 Leagues Under the Sea）和“乡村熊乐园”（Country Bear Jamboree）表演。“海底两万里”

cues.en: consistently sat at one hour, and the wait for the Country Bear Jamboree could go over an hour on busier days. This might be surprising to you if you visited the parks recently. Today, the Country Bear Jamboree almost never fills its theater, and 20000 Leagues no longer exists. However, when Magic Kingdom opened, these two attractions had some of the longest waits in the park. This can be explained by looking at the arrival rate and service rate of these attractions.
cues.zh: 的排队时间一直稳定在一个小时，而在客流量较大的日子里，“乡村熊乐园”的排队时间甚至会超过一个小时。如果你最近去过这些乐园，这可能会让你感到意外。如今，“乡村熊乐园”几乎从未坐满过剧场，“海底两万里”也已不复存在。然而，当神奇王国刚开业时，这两个项目曾是乐园里排队时间最长的项目之一。这可以通过分析这些项目的到达率和接待率来解释。

cues.en: The service rate for theme park attractions is generally measured in hourly capacity,
cues.zh: 主题乐园项目的接待率通常以每小时的载客量来衡量，

cues.en: or how many guests can board an attraction within one hour. 20,000
cues.zh: 即一小时内能有多少游客登上游乐设施。“海底两万里”

cues.en: was a low capacity attraction, only able to accommodate around 1,200 guests per hour. Compare this to the Haunted Mansion, which can accommodate around 2,800
cues.zh: 是一个低容量项目，每小时只能接待大约1200名游客。相比之下，“幽灵公馆”每小时可以接待大约2800名

cues.en: guests per hour. This difference was due to their ride systems. The Haunted Mansion is a continuously operating omnimover system, while 20,000 leagues can only seat 40 guests in each submarine and could only operate up to nine submarines at a time. So in a twelve hour day at the park, over 33,000
cues.zh: 游客。这种差异是由它们的运载系统造成的。“幽灵公馆”是一个持续运行的环形全景车（omnimover）系统，而“海底两万里”每艘潜艇只能坐40名游客，且同时最多只能运行9艘潜艇。因此，在乐园运营的12小时内，

cues.en: guests could ride the Haunted Mansion, while only around 14,000 guests could ride 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea. Looking at this difference another way, if 1,000 guests were in line for both attractions,
cues.zh: 有超过33,000名游客可以体验“幽灵公馆”，而只有大约14,000名游客能够体验“海底两万里”。换个角度来看这种差异，如果两个项目的排队队伍中都有1000名游客，

cues.en: the wait time for the Haunted Mansion would be thirty five minutes, while the wait time for 20,000 Leagues would be one hour and twenty minutes.
cues.zh: 那么“幽灵公馆”的等待时间将是35分钟，而“海底两万里”的等待时间将是一个小时零二十分钟。

cues.en: The Country Bear Jamboree had an even lower capacity than 20,000 leagues, but its issue was less in its service rate and more in its arrival rate. While the capacity of a ride is determined by design and operation,
cues.zh: 乡村熊俱乐部（Country Bear Jamboree）的载客量甚至比“海底两万里”还要低，但它的问题不在于服务速率，而在于客流量的到达率。虽然游乐设施的容量由设计和运营决定，

cues.en: the arrival rate is mainly determined by guest demand. This demand can be influenced by such factors as the quality of the ride and the marketing done for the attraction.
cues.zh: 但到达率主要取决于游客的需求。这种需求会受到游乐设施的质量以及景点的营销等因素的影响。

cues.en: The demand and capacity relationship is somewhat similar to the relationship between the supply and demand of a product, except rather than determining price and quantity, demand and capacity determine wait times and number of riders.
cues.zh: 需求和容量的关系有点类似于商品的供求关系，只不过需求和容量决定的不是价格和数量，而是等待时间和乘车人数。

cues.en: Today, once a guest has entered a Disney theme park, they are able to ride any attraction they choose, but there are only so many operating hours each day, so time becomes a currency that they must spend. For instance, a guest might want to ride the jungle cruise if the wait were thirty minutes, but that same guest might not want to ride the attraction if the wait was one hour. In queuing, this is called bulking, when someone decides not to wait in a queue due to its length. This can reduce wait times by turning people away that were not determined to experience the attraction. The situation becomes even more complicated when guests are spending both their time and money to ride rides.
cues.zh: 今天，游客一旦进入迪士尼主题公园，就可以游玩他们选择的任何项目，但每天的运营时间是有限的，因此时间成了他们必须花掉的货币。例如，如果等待时间是三十分钟，游客可能会想去玩丛林巡航，但如果等待时间是一个小时，同一个游客可能就不想去玩这个项目了。在排队论中，这被称为拒绝排队（bulking），即由于队伍太长而决定不排队。通过将那些并非一定要体验该景点的游客劝退，这可以减少等待时间。当游客既要花时间又要花钱来玩游乐设施时，情况就会变得更加复杂。

cues.en: When it opened, Walt Disney World utilized a ticket book system, in which guests needed to purchase tickets both to enter the park and to ride the majority of the park's attractions, with each attraction distinguished with a letter a through e, with e being the most thrilling and popular attractions.
cues.zh: 沃尔特迪士尼世界开业时采用了一种门票册系统，游客需要购票才能进入园区，乘坐园区大多数游乐设施也需要购票，每个游乐设施用字母a到e来区分，其中e代表最刺激、最受欢迎的游乐设施。

cues.en: This was the same system used at Disneyland,
cues.zh: 这与迪士尼乐园使用的系统相同，

cues.en: and it became so well known that the term e ticket became a common phrase to refer to something as premium or exciting.
cues.zh: 它变得如此广为人知，以至于e ticket这个词成了常用说法，用来指代高端或令人兴奋的事物。

cues.en: By charging guests more to ride the popular attractions, Disneyland was able to curb demand for these rides.
cues.zh: 通过对热门游乐设施收取更高的费用，迪士尼乐园得以抑制这些游乐设施的需求。

cues.en: However, at Walt Disney World, this system often had the opposite effect. When the resort opened, guests knew little about the park's unique attractions,
cues.zh: 然而，在沃尔特迪士尼世界，这套系统往往产生了相反的效果。度假区开业时，游客对园区独特的游乐设施知之甚少，

cues.en: but they already understood the a through e ticket system. So when visitors made their decisions, they often looked at how Disney ranked and priced their own attractions.
cues.zh: 但他们已经理解了a到e的门票系统。所以当游客做选择时，他们往往看迪士尼如何给自己的游乐设施分级和定价。

cues.en: The Country Bear Jamboree,
cues.zh: 乡村熊俱乐部，

cues.en: a musical show with animatronic characters unknown to guests, was listed as an E ticket, while the Mickey Mouse Review, a musical show with animatronic characters well known to guests, was listed as a D ticket. This led many guests to assume that the Country Bear Jamboree was the better show, resulting in a false demand leading to longer lines. This false demand was recognized by a Disney employee named Bruce Laval. Laval graduated from the University of Florida with an MBA specializing in operations research, and he joined Walt Disney World right as the resort opened in 1971
cues.zh: 一场游客并不熟悉的电子动画角色音乐秀，被列为E ticket，而米奇老鼠大汇演，一场游客熟知的电子动画角色音乐秀，被列为D ticket。这让许多游客以为乡村熊俱乐部是更好的演出，从而产生了虚假需求，导致排队更长。这种虚假需求被一位名叫Bruce Laval的迪士尼员工注意到了。Laval毕业于佛罗里达大学，获得运筹学方向的MBA学位，他在1971年度假区开业之际加入了沃尔特迪士尼世界，

cues.en: as an industrial engineer. Industrial engineers are specialized in studying and optimizing complex systems and processes,
cues.zh: 担任工业工程师。工业工程师专门研究和优化复杂系统与流程，

cues.en: finding ways to make systems more efficient, a field that Disney was increasingly relying on as their theme parks became more complex and brought in more people. Laval was among the first industrial engineers to utilize computer simulations to optimize systems. Impressive, considering at the time, computers looked like this.
cues.zh: 寻找让系统更高效的方法，随着主题公园变得越来越复杂、吸引越来越多的人，迪士尼越来越依赖这一领域。Laval是最早利用计算机模拟来优化系统的工业工程师之一。考虑到当时的计算机长这样，这相当了不起。

cues.en: Within the first few years he worked for the company, Laval noticed the false demand being created by the a through e ticket system and argued for its removal. The idea made it almost to the testing phase for Magic Kingdom, when top Disney executives,
cues.zh: 在为公司工作的最初几年里，Laval 注意到 A 到 E 票制正在制造虚假需求，并主张取消它。这个想法几乎推进到了 Magic Kingdom 的测试阶段，就在这时迪士尼高层，

cues.en: resistant to change, learned of the plan and shut it down. However, it was soon decided that Disney's third theme park, Epcot Center, would not use the a three ticket system, so the decision was made to discontinue the system at both Disneyland and Walt Disney World as well. After the switch, Laval's theory was proven. Wait times at e tickets went down and more guests visited the underutilized attractions.
cues.zh: 抵制变革，得知该计划后将其叫停。然而，很快决定迪士尼的第三个主题公园——艾波卡特中心——不采用三票制，因此决定在迪士尼乐园和沃尔特迪士尼世界也停止该制度。切换之后，拉瓦尔的理论得到了验证。E票的等待时间下降，更多游客参观了利用率不足的景点。

cues.en: Long lines were by no means eliminated from the guest experience after the a three e ticket system was discontinued.
cues.zh: 在三E票务系统停用之后，游客体验中的长队现象远未消除。

cues.en: In fact, lines were the number one guest complaint at all three Disney parks. This is why when Disney opened its first international park, Tokyo Disneyland,
cues.zh: 事实上，排队问题曾是迪士尼三大乐园游客投诉的头号问题。正因如此，当迪士尼开设首个国际乐园——东京迪士尼乐园时，

cues.en: many within the company were surprised at the patience and endurance of Japanese tourists to withstand long lines,
cues.zh: 公司里很多人都惊讶于日本游客忍受长队的耐心和耐力，

cues.en: especially when compared to Americans.
cues.zh: 尤其是跟美国人相比的时候。

cues.en: This is because different cultures have different reactions to queuing, with Americans tending to be some of the most impatient, right up there with the French, which Disney would learn soon enough. Also, people's reactions to queues change significantly over time, and the Disney parks have played a major role in this evolution. The most common type of queue at Disney is called the switchback queue, in which guests snake back and forth in a zigzag motion. This was pioneered by Disney's Imagineers at the nineteen sixty four New York World's Fair. The lines for Disney's attractions at the fair were long and out of control, so Disney developed the Switchback concept, which organized and condensed the line. Reportedly, Walt Disney himself also felt the concept had a psychological benefit. Because guests were moving back and forth, they were face to face with other guests, allowing them to interact with strangers back when people were into that sort of thing. Switchback queues were soon implemented throughout Disneyland,
cues.zh: 这是因为不同文化对排队的反应不同，美国人往往是最不耐烦的群体之一，和法国人一样，这一点迪士尼很快就领教了。此外，人们对排队的反应会随时间发生显著变化，而迪士尼乐园在这一演变中发挥了重要作用。迪士尼最常见的排队类型叫折返式排队，客人以之字形来回蜿蜒前进。这最早由迪士尼幻想工程师在1964年纽约世界博览会上开创。博览会上迪士尼游乐项目的队伍又长又失控，于是迪士尼开发了折返式概念，把队伍组织并压缩起来。据说沃尔特·迪士尼本人也认为这个概念有心理上的好处。因为客人们来回走动时会面对面，能和其他客人互动，在那个人们还喜欢这种事的年代。折返式排队很快就在迪士尼乐园全面推行，

cues.en: then at Walt Disney World, Epcot Center, and eventually everywhere.
cues.zh: 然后是在华特迪士尼世界、艾波卡特中心，最终无处不在。

cues.en: But since queuing is always evolving, by the mid nineteen eighties, distaste for the Switchback queue had grown. People were no longer tricked by its condensed nature, and the endless zigzagging soon became grating. To combat this, Disney went back to the drawing board, coming up with a simple three tiered strategy to improve guest time in line. Number one, keep waits to a maximum of fifteen minutes. Number two, if a guest must wait more than fifteen minutes, give them entertainment, such as immersive queues and pre show videos. Number three, hide the queue from view, sectioning off different parts of the queue so the guests can't see how long the line really is until they've already waited in it. This strategy really came down to one basic principle. If you remove the guest's ability to visualize the wait, the wait itself will feel shorter.
cues.zh: 但由于排队方式总是在演到，到了八十年代中期，人们对“回折式”排队的厌恶日益增加。大家不再被它紧凑的外表所蒙蔽，那无休止的“之”字形排队很快让人感到烦躁。为了解决这个问题，迪士尼重新回到图纸前，想出了一套简单的三层策略来改善游客的排队时间。第一，将等待时间控制在最多十五分钟。第二，如果游客不得不等待超过十五分钟，就提供娱乐，比如沉浸式排队区和预演视频。第三，将排队队伍隐藏起来，把排队区划分成不同部分，这样游客在真正排进去之前，根本看不到队伍到底有多长。这个策略其实归结为一个基本原则：如果你消除了游客对等待时间的直观感受，等待本身就会显得更短。

cues.en: In 1987, Bruce Laval was named the director of the studio tour for the soon to open Disney MGM Studios.
cues.zh: 1987年，Bruce Laval 被任命为即将开业的迪士尼米高梅影城的园区游览总监。

cues.en: The new theme park was designed to focus primarily on the tour of the new film and television production facilities being constructed alongside the park. So when Disney MGM opened in 1989,
cues.zh: 这座新主题公园的设计初衷，主要是围绕公园旁正在建设的新电影和电视制作设施进行参观。因此，当迪士尼米高梅在1989年开业时，

cues.en: it had few attractions,
cues.zh: 它只有极少数的景点，

cues.en: and worse, few productions.
cues.zh: 更糟糕的是，几乎没什么制作项目。

cues.en: What it did have was an excess of people. Crowds flocked to Disney MGM to find long lines and little to do. The issue was widely reported on, and when asked about the crowds, Laval said, quote, you could have the greatest show in the world, but if you have a three hour wait out there, people are going to leave the park dissatisfied.
cues.zh: 它真正有的是过剩的人流。大批游客涌入迪士尼米高梅，结果发现长龙阵阵、无事可做。这个问题被广泛报道，当被问及人群时，Laval 说道：“你可以拥有世界上最棒的演出，但如果外面要排三个小时的队，人们离开时还是会对公园感到不满。”

cues.en: Immediately after the article was published, the Orlando Sentinel received a call from a man named Michael Eisner, who was the CEO of Disney at the time. Eisner assured the public, as well as the Disney employees quoted in Sunday's paper, that the park would be expanded with more attractions, stating, quote, we do not want the lines to be that long. We are trying to rectify that as soon as we can. In 1995,
cues.zh: 文章发表后不久，《奥兰多哨兵报》接到了一名叫做Michael Eisner的男子的电话，他当时是迪士尼的CEO。Eisner向公众以及周日报纸中被引述的迪士尼员工向公众保证，乐园将会扩建更多的游乐设施，他原话表示：“我们不希望排队时间那么长。我们正在努力尽快纠正这一点。”在1995年，

cues.en: Laval was promoted to executive vice president of operations, now assuming responsibility for all park and resort operations at the Disney parks. Laval had held many different positions at the company, but his industrial engineering background had stayed with and the mounting issues with wait times led Laval and his team to develop something big.
cues.zh: Laval被晋升为运营执行副总裁，现在负责迪士尼乐园所有的公园和度假区运营。Laval在公司担任过许多不同的职位，但他的工业工程背景一直伴随着他，不断增加的等待时间问题促使Laval和他的团队开发了一项重磅成果。

cues.en: In
cues.zh: 在

cues.en: the mid nineteen nineties, Laval and his team began experimenting with the idea of transitioning certain attractions at the Disney parks to a reservation only system. The idea was to give guests a reservation time for an attraction, so that they would not have to wait in line. Similar to a restaurant, guests would simply arrive at the attraction for the reservation and would be seated immediately.
cues.zh: 20世纪90年代中期，Laval和他的团队开始尝试将迪士尼乐园的某些游乐设施过渡到仅限预约的系统的想法。这个想法是为游客提供游乐设施的预约时间，这样他们就不必排队了。类似于餐厅，游客只需在预约时间到达游乐设施即可立即就座。

cues.en: While the idea would eliminate waits for guests at the park's most popular attractions,
cues.zh: 虽然这个想法可以消除游客在乐园最受欢迎的游乐设施前的等待时间，

cues.en: there were obvious issues with the concept. First, it was nearly impossible to ensure that park guests arrived for their reservations on time. Often, they would be doing something else around the park. When a guest would miss their reservation time, this would leave empty seats on the ride, therefore reducing the total capacity of the attraction.
cues.zh: 但这个概念存在明显的缺陷。首先，几乎无法确保乐园游客准时到达预约地点。通常，他们会在乐园的其他地方做别的事情。当游客错过预约时间时，这会导致游乐设施出现空位，从而降低了该景点的总承载能力。

cues.en: Second, if the attraction experienced downtime for any reason, then the guests holding reservations during this downtime would no longer be able to ride, as reservations for the rest of the day would already be filled. Or if they were allowed on, the ride would now have a line of people for the rest of the day, defeating the point of the system. The idea was abandoned for these reasons, and it seemed that reservation based attractions was a dead concept.
cues.zh:
其次，如果游乐设施因任何原因停运，那么停运期间持有预约的游客就无法乘坐，因为当天剩余时段的预约早已订满。
或者，即使允许他们乘坐，项目当天剩下的时间也会排起长队，这就违背了这套系统的初衷。
因此，这个想法被放弃了，预约制游乐项目似乎也成了过时的概念。

cues.en: This was until Laval had an epiphany, not while at work, but while on vacation.
cues.zh: 直到 Laval 灵光一闪，不是在工作时，而是在度假的时候。

cues.en: Laval went on a skiing vacation in Colorado.
cues.zh: Laval 去科罗拉多滑雪度假了。

cues.en: While on the slopes, he observed the queue to get on the ski lift. Each lift chair held four people, and the queue was split into two lines, a regular line and a single rider line. Laval viewed how the single riders were squeezed into the empty seats on the ski lift when a party did not fill an entire chair. He realized that this was the compromise to the reservation based system. Rather than a regular line and a single rider line, Laval can have a reservation based system and a standby line. Whenever a guest would be late for the reservation, operators could take someone from the standby line so that the attraction would never lose capacity because of the ebbs and flows in guest behavior. Plus, if the attraction did experience downtime,
cues.zh: 他在雪道上观察排队上滑雪缆车的人。每张缆车吊椅坐四个人，队伍分成两列：普通队列和单人乘客队列。Laval 看到，当一行人没有坐满整张吊椅时，单人乘客会被安排进滑雪缆车的空座。他意识到，这就是对预约制的一种妥协。Laval 可以不用普通队列和单人乘客队列，而是采用预约制加候补队列。每当有客人预约迟到，运营人员就可以从候补队列中补人，这样游乐项目就不会因为客人行为的波动而损失接待容量。另外，如果游乐项目确实出现停运，

cues.en: then the ratio of reservation based guests to standby riders could simply be adjusted to favor those that had reservations during the downtime. Despite the idea coming from the initial reservation based concept, what Laval was proposing was closer to a virtual queue. A virtual queue functions similarly to a normal queue, just without the physical line. A common example of a virtual queue can be found in many quick service restaurants,
cues.zh: 那么，预约客人与候补乘客的比例可以简单调整，以便在停运期间优先照顾已预约的人。尽管这个想法源自最初的预约制概念，但Laval提出的方案更接近于虚拟队列。虚拟队列的运作方式与普通队列类似，只是没有实体队伍。虚拟队列的一个常见例子可以在许多快餐店中找到，

cues.en: in which guests take a number and wait for their number to be called. Unlike reservations, this still retains the first come, first served nature of a physical line, but it removes the ability to visualize the wait, therefore increasing the quality of it. After returning from vacation, Laval pitched the concept to other executives, but he was met with skepticism.
cues.zh: 顾客取一个号码，等待叫号。与预订不同，这种方式仍保留实体排队的先到先得特性，但不再让人直观看到等待情况，从而提升了等待体验。度假回来后，Laval 向其他高管推介这个想法，却遭到了怀疑。

cues.en: Believing in the idea, Laval proposed that he test the concept to prove that it could work. Using the newly opened Animal Kingdom due to its limited amount of attractions, testing began with a select group of guests who were given paper diaries to keep track of their day, including how long they waited in line. The test subjects were split into two groups, a control group and a group that would use the virtual queue system. The control group simply logged their day at the park, while the other group were told to approach cast members at attraction entrances, who would hand them a ticket with a return time on it. This return time was equal to the time that it would have taken guests to wait in line for the ride. The test subjects were then encouraged to explore the park and return at the time listed on the ticket, where they would then be allowed to skip the line. The test was a huge success. The virtual queue subjects were able to experience 25% more rides than the control group, and their wait times were reduced by 50%.
cues.zh: 出于对这个想法的信心，Laval 提议对这一概念进行测试，以证明其可行性。由于新开业的 Animal Kingdom 游乐项目较少，测试便选在这里展开；他们挑选了一组游客，并给他们发放了纸质日记本，用来记录一天的行程，包括排队等候的时长。测试对象被分成两组：一组是对照组，另一组则使用虚拟排队系统。对照组只需记录在乐园的一天，而另一组则被告知前往项目入口联系工作人员，工作人员会发给他们一张写有返回时间的票。这个返回时间等于游客正常排队玩该项目所需的时间。随后，受试者被鼓励去乐园其他地方游玩，并在票上标注的时间返回，届时他们就可以免去排队直接进入。测试取得了巨大的成功。使用虚拟排队的受试者体验的项目比对照组多了 25%，而他们的排队时间缩短了 50%。

cues.en: The virtual queue subjects left the park much more satisfied and far more likely to return than the control group. If this was not convincing enough for executives,
cues.zh: 使用虚拟队列的受试者离开公园时满意度更高，回访意愿也远超对照组。如果这还不足以说服管理层，

cues.en: the tests also showed that those using the virtual queue system spent more of their time at gift shops and dining locations,
cues.zh: 测试还显示，使用虚拟排队系统的人花更多时间在礼品店和餐饮场所，

cues.en: resulting in more spending when compared to the control group. Executives approved the concept for further testing, which continued throughout early nineteen ninety nine, both at Disneyland and Walt Disney World. That summer, testing focused on Space Mountain at the Magic Kingdom, which often had the park's longest wait. In these early tests, cast members were physically writing return times on cards and giving them to guests, while using handheld clicker counters to keep track of how many were handed out and how many guests returned.
cues.zh: 与对照组相比，这带来了更多消费。高管批准了这一概念进行进一步测试，测试在整个1999年初持续进行，覆盖迪士尼乐园和华特迪士尼世界。那年夏天，测试集中在魔法王国的太空山，那里常有园区最长的排队等待。在这些早期测试中，演职人员会手动把返回时间写在卡片上发给游客，同时用手持计数器记录发出了多少张、有多少游客返回。

cues.en: The tests were often haphazard and chaotic, but they were successful enough to prove that not only the system could work, but it would make guests happier and more likely to spend money. Many within the company, including Laval, felt that the system should be free and available to all visitors so as not to create different classes of park guests, citing Walt Disney himself, who was known to wait in the park's lines with his guests. With the test labeled a success, executives approved the permanent installation of the new virtual queue system, officially titled...
cues.zh: 这些测试往往随意而混乱，但已经足够成功，证明了系统不仅可行，还能让游客更开心、更愿意花钱。公司内部许多人，包括Laval，都认为该系统应该免费向所有游客开放，以免造成园区游客的等级分化，并引用了Walt Disney本人的做法——他以和游客一起在园区排队等候而闻名。测试被认定为成功，高管们批准永久安装这套新的虚拟排队系统，正式名称为……

cues.en: Hey.
cues.zh: 嘿。

cues.en: Did you know that you don't have to wait in line to ride some of your favorite attractions?
cues.zh: 你知道有些热门项目其实不用排队吗？

cues.en: Just look for the signs of selected attractions and insert your park ticket.
cues.zh: 只要找到指定项目的标志，插入你的园区门票。

cues.en: You'll get a complimentary FastPass
cues.zh: 你就能获得一张免费的FastPass

cues.en: with the return ride time stamped right on it. Guests who entered a Walt Disney World park in late nineteen ninety nine were met with a brand new system, FastPass.
cues.zh: 上面印有返回乘坐时间。1999年末进入Walt Disney World园区的游客，迎来了一套全新的系统——FastPass。

cues.en: On the surface, the system was simple. Guests would approach an attraction where they would be able to view the posted standby wait time. If this was manageable, they could join the standby queue right away. However, if the wait was too long, they could instead choose to receive a FastPass at the kiosks placed outside of the attractions.
cues.zh: 表面上看，这套系统很简单。游客来到某个项目前，可以查看公布的 standby 等候时间。如果时间可以接受，他们可以直接加入 standby 队列。但如果等候时间太长，他们也可以选择在项目外的自助机上领取FastPass。

cues.en: Guests inserted their park admission ticket into the kiosk to receive their FastPass with a one hour return window listed on it. They could then enjoy the rest of the park, and once the return window arrived, they would hand their ticket to an attendant and enter the FastPass queue, boarding the attraction with a minimal wait. Each guest could only hold one FastPass at a time, and they could not receive another until the return window had arrived. Behind the scenes, the system was far more complex.
cues.zh: 游客将入园门票插入自助机，领取印有一小时返回窗口的FastPass。之后他们可以继续游玩园区其他地方，等返回窗口到了，把门票交给工作人员，进入FastPass队列，几乎无需等待即可乘坐项目。每位游客一次只能持有一张FastPass，且在返回窗口到来之前不能再领取。而在幕后，这套系统要复杂得多。

cues.en: Each attraction's FastPass data would be stored on a local computer housed in each attraction, controlling the standby wait time display, keeping track of how many FastPasses have been handed out, and determining the return times being printed on each FastPass. The computer was connected to a server so all wait times could be monitored throughout the park, and so that the system would know when a guest had already been given a FastPass to prevent them from obtaining another.
cues.zh: 每个景点的 FastPass 数据都存储在各景点内的本地计算机上，用来控制排队等待时间的显示、追踪已发放的 FastPass 数量，并决定每张 FastPass 上打印的返场时间。这台计算机连接到一个服务器，以便在整个园区监控所有等待时间，并让系统知道游客是否已经拿过 FastPass，从而防止他们重复获取。

cues.en: The system also allowed ride operators to tell the computer when an attraction was experiencing downtime,
cues.zh: 该系统还允许游乐设施操作员在景点发生故障时通知计算机，

cues.en: and in response, the kiosk would slow down or cease dispersing fast passes until the attraction was operating again. Some cast members reported this feature not working properly or not implemented on some rides, resulting in ride operators having to go to the Fast Pass kiosk, manually disperse a stack of paper Fast Passes so that return times were pushed back, and then immediately throw those Fast Passes in the trash. When news broke on FastPass in the summer of nineteen ninety nine, Laval said, quote, we are going to use it on three, four, or five attractions that historically have the longest slides at each park. By the end of the year, 13 attractions at Walt Disney World utilized FastPass.
cues.zh: 作为响应，自助机将会减慢或停止发放 FastPass，直到景点恢复运营。一些演职人员反映，该功能在部分游乐设施上无法正常工作甚至根本没有实现，导致操作员不得不走到 FastPass 自助机前，手动发放一叠纸质 FastPass 以推迟返场时间，然后立即将这些 FastPass 扔进垃圾桶。1999 年夏天的 FastPass 新闻曝光后，Laval 表示：“我们打算在每个公园历来排队时间最长的三、四个或五个景点上使用它。”到年底时，华特迪士尼世界的 13 个景点都使用了 FastPass。

cues.en: Five at Magic Kingdom, two at Epcot, five at Disney MGM, and three at Animal Kingdom. In early two thousand, FastPass was implemented in Disneyland on three attractions,
cues.zh: 其中神奇王国 5 个、艾泼科特 2 个、迪士尼米高梅 5 个、动物王国 3 个。2000 年初，迪士尼乐园在 3 个景点推出了 FastPass，

cues.en: Space Mountain, Splash Mountain, and Roger Rabbit's cartoon spin, with plans to expand the program.
cues.zh: 即太空山、飞溅山和罗杰兔卡通转转车，并计划进一步扩大该项目。

cues.en: One way to keep it moving is called Disney's Fast Pass. Me, Un, Faberito.
cues.zh: 让队伍持续流动的一种方法叫迪士尼的 FastPass。我、Un、Faberito。

cues.en: Check this out. You roll up to the Fast Pass kiosk. Boom. Boom. Kicks back ride time. Then you just come back to the ride at that time and giddy up. Pretty sweet little invention. Let's hit it. FastPass was a huge learning curve for guests. Despite heavy marketing, many guests did not know about the program and even fewer understood it. In the early days, it was referred to as Disney's best kept secret, and many guests waiting in standby lines were visibly and vocally frustrated to see priority being given to those that had fast passes, believing that they were being skipped or cut in line, which in a way, they were. Some people believe that Fastpass was simply holding their place in the attractions line, which is not the case. The Fastpass kiosk and ticket system was a virtual queue, so there was a first come first served system built into the program, but that just determined guest return windows. Once guests redeemed their pass, that queue was over and they were admitted to a new preferred queue that shared the service rate of the attraction with the standby line. The arrival of Fastpass guests did affect the rate at which guests moved through the standby queue. There were a few exceptions to this, such as with Space Mountain at the Magic Kingdom, which has two separate tracks. So if operated as such, one track could be standby only, and the other could be fast pass only. If this is the case, then fast pass guests are not skipping or cutting the standby line, They essentially just have their own attraction, as there are two separate service rates, and the arrival of FastPass guests have no impact on the standby line. The main issues with implementing FastPass beyond the learning curve for guests was perfecting the technology for the kiosks and finding space in each attraction for two lines. Luckily, many attractions already had two lines, and guests were given the choice of either the left line or the right line when they entered. A common advice from vacation planners was to always go left because the majority of people are right handed and thus tended to go right, a phenomenon found outside of Disney's parks and studied by queuing experts for some time. Some attractions already had a split point, but not until later on in their queue. For instance, Space Mountain at Walt Disney World had a wide single line hallway up to the ramp leading to the main show building. Here, a railing was added and all guests had to go to the right side, so that cast members could walk on the left. This made installing FastPass fairly simple, because Disney only needed to extend the railing the beginning of the queue and build a staircase to the entrance so the left side and the right side remained split the entire time. Reviews from those guests that used fast pass were overwhelmingly positive.
cues.zh: 看这个。你走到 FastPass 自助机前。砰。砰。它吐出乘坐时间。到点你再回到项目，直接开玩。挺不错的小发明。走起。对游客来说，FastPass 的学习成本很高。尽管做了大量宣传，很多游客仍不知道这个项目，真正理解的人更少。早期它被称为迪士尼“保守得最好的秘密”。许多在普通队列里排队的游客，看到持 FastPass 的人被优先放行，明显又大声地表达不满，觉得自己被插队或被跳过了——某种程度上确实如此。有些人以为 FastPass 只是在游乐设施队列里帮他们占位，事实并非如此。FastPass 自助机和票务系统是一个虚拟队列，所以项目内置了先到先得机制，但这只决定游客的返回时间窗。游客核销通行证后，那个队列就结束了，他们被放进一个新的优先队列，与普通队列共享该设施的服务速率。FastPass 游客的到来确实会影响普通队列游客的前进速度。也有少数例外，比如魔法王国的太空山有两条独立轨道。若按这种方式运营，一条轨道可以只给普通队列，另一条只给 FastPass。若真是这样，FastPass 游客就不是在跳过或插普通队列；他们本质上只是有了自己的游乐设施，因为存在两个独立的服务速率，FastPass 游客的到来不会影响普通队列。实施 FastPass 的主要问题，除了游客的学习成本，就是完善自助机技术，并在每个设施里找到两条队列的空间。幸运的是，很多设施本来就有两条队列，游客入口时可选择左道或右道。度假规划师常建议总是走左边，因为多数人是右撇子，因而倾向走右边；这种现象在迪士尼乐园外也能看到，排队专家已经研究了一段时间。有些设施已经有分流点，但直到队列较后段才分流。例如，华特迪士尼世界的太空山有一条宽大的单列走廊，通向主展演建筑的坡道。这里加了一道栏杆，所有游客都必须走右侧，好让演职人员走左侧。这让安装 FastPass 变得相当简单，因为迪士尼只需把栏杆延伸到队列起点，并建一段通向入口的楼梯，让左右两侧全程保持分流。使用 FastPass 的游客评价压倒性地正面。

cues.en: On average, guests that utilized system waited 75%
cues.zh: 平均而言，使用该系统的游客全天等待时间减少了75%。

cues.en: less throughout the day. A few skeptics believed that the system would increase standby weight significantly throughout the park. Laval responded to this concern saying, quote, it's only a problem if they don't self select. The only challenge has been getting people to understand Fast Pass. He added that, quote, people go on to what you might consider the secondary attractions in that area of the ride they have FastPass for. We found that these were typically attractions that they didn't go on before because they were spending too much time in line. This does increase rides per capita by backfilling less attended attractions.
cues.zh: 少数怀疑者认为，该系统会显著增加整个园区的普通排队负担。Laval对此回应说：“只有游客不自行选择时才会成为问题。”唯一的挑战是让人们理解Fast Pass。他补充说：“游客会去玩你可能认为该区域次要的游乐项目，因为他们有FastPass。我们发现这些通常是他们以前不玩的游乐项目，因为他们花太多时间排队。这确实通过填充人气较低的游乐项目提高了人均乘坐次数。”

cues.en: FastPass also had the potential, in certain situations, to reduce standby wait times because it altered the arrival rate of popular attractions. By giving guests return windows, it spread out arrivals more evenly throughout the day, flattening the midday rush and reducing standby waits during this peak period. Those that loved Fastpass argued that the system should be added to all of the rides in the park. Dale Stafford, VP of Operations Planning and Development for Walt Disney World, believed that this was not practical, saying, quote, if you did it everywhere, you wouldn't have enough space in the park. Where would everyone go?
cues.zh: 在某些情况下，FastPass还有可能减少普通排队等待时间，因为它改变了热门游乐项目的到达率。通过给游客返回时间窗口，它使到达更均匀地分布在全天，平抑了午间高峰，并减少了这一高峰时段的普通排队等待。喜欢FastPass的人认为，该系统应加到园区所有游乐项目上。Walt Disney World运营规划与开发副总裁Dale Stafford认为这不切实际，他说：“如果到处都这样做，园区里就没有足够空间了。大家去哪儿呢？”

cues.en: One year after FastPass was introduced, both guests and Disney officials were confident in labeling the program a massive success. Eisner said, quote, they now have more time to spend money and to do other things. They're also a lot happier not having to wait in line. In August 2000, FastPass was recognized by the Florida Engineering Society and was awarded a 2000 Governor's New Product Award. Laval said, quote, FastPass continues to exceed our guest expectations.
cues.zh: FastPass 推出一年后，游客和 Disney 高层都确信该项目取得了巨大成功。Eisner 表示：“他们现在有更多时间花钱和做其他事情了。不用排队也让他们开心得多。”2000 年 8 月，FastPass 获得了 Florida Engineering Society 的认可，并荣获 2000 年度 Governor's New Product Award。Laval 表示：“FastPass 一直在超出游客的预期。

cues.en: It's a free service and it's making their time in the parks more fun and productive. Laval retired in 2000 after thirty years with the company, with FastPass being his last major project.
cues.zh: 这是一项免费服务，让游客在乐园里玩得更开心、更充实。”Laval 在公司工作 30 年后于 2000 年退休，FastPass 是他最后一个重大项目。

cues.en: Perhaps the greatest success of FastPass was the name. It was catchy and concise,
cues.zh: 也许 FastPass 最大的成功在于它的名字。它朗朗上口且简明扼要，

cues.en: so much so that it immediately became a household name and a colloquialism
cues.zh: 以至于迅速家喻户晓，并成为一种代名词，

cues.en: for any sort of expedited line. It also pushed other parks to develop their own expedited queue systems, and it even inspired a hit song.
cues.zh: 用来代指任何类型的快速通道。它还促使其他乐园开发自己的快速排队系统，甚至还催生了一首热门歌曲。

cues.en: It was not long until touring experts started to learn the best practices for the FastPass system.
cues.zh: 没过多久，游玩达人们就开始摸索出 FastPass 系统的最佳游玩攻略。

cues.en: For instance, guests still needed to arrive earlier in the day to receive FastPasses with optimal return times. If a guest arrived at the park's opening, they could receive a FastPass with the return window only an hour away. However, by midday, many FastPass return times could be four to five hours in the future, and on busier days, FastPasses for popular attractions would run out by one or 02:00 in the afternoon. While the system itself worked well, there were a few issues. One was the decision to not allow guests to receive another FastPass until the return window arrived. This left many guests upset when they went to get a FastPass for an attraction, only to realize that the return window was hours away and they could not get another FastPass until then. The solution to this was allowing guests to receive an additional FastPass two hours after receiving their initial one. Some less than honest guests found that they could simply keep their FastPasses from previous days or trips and reuse them over and over again. To combat this, Disney changed the design of FastPass tickets to more clearly show the date, although this did not entirely curb the practice.
cues.zh: 例如，游客仍需在一大早就入园，才能领到返场时间最理想的 FastPass。如果游客一开园就到，领到的 FastPass 返场窗口期可能只在一小时之后。然而到了中午，很多 FastPass 的返场时间可能就是四五个小时之后了；而在客流较大的日子里，热门项目的 FastPass 到下午一两点就会被抢光。尽管系统本身运转良好，但也存在一些问题。其中之一就是规定游客在当前返场窗口到达前不能领取下一张 FastPass。这让很多游客很不爽：当他们去领某个项目的 FastPass 时，才发现返场时间在几小时之后，而在此之前他们都领不了下一张。对此的解决办法是允许游客在领取上一张 FastPass 两小时后即可领取下一张。还有一些投机取巧的游客发现，他们只需保留之前几天或历次游玩时的 FastPass，就能反复多次使用。为了解决这个问题，Disney 重新设计了 FastPass 票面，更醒目地标注日期，但这并没有彻底杜绝这种现象。

cues.en: Others found ways to best the system to get as many FastPasses as possible. Guests found that some attractions did not communicate with the rest of the park's computers. So if they were to get a FastPass from one of these rogue attractions, they would not communicate that the guest already held a FastPass, and they could therefore obtain another. Fast pass kiosks were also used in creative ways. For instance, guests obtaining a fast pass for Who Wants to Be a Millionaire Play It might have received a special ticket inviting them to sit in one of the special contestant seats at the attraction.
cues.zh: 其他人则想方设法钻系统的空子，尽可能多地获取 FastPass。游客们发现，有些游乐设施并没有与乐园里其他计算机联网。因此，如果他们从这些“野路子”游乐设施拿到一张 FastPass，系统就不会记录游客已经持有一张 FastPass，于是他们就能再拿一张。FastPass 自助机也被玩出了各种花样。例如，游客在为《谁想成为百万富翁：游戏版》（Who Wants to Be a Millionaire Play It）获取 FastPass 时，可能会拿到一张特殊的门票，邀请他们去坐该项目专属的选手席。

cues.en: Sometimes the kiosks were used to direct people to other attractions by giving them a bonus FastPass,
cues.zh: 有时，自助机会通过赠送奖励 FastPass 来将人流引导至其他游乐设施，

cues.en: such as The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh, which sometimes dispense bonus FastPasses for Mickey's Philhar magic. On 02/17/2003,
cues.zh: 比如《小熊维尼历险记》（The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh），有时会发放用于《米奇幻想曲》（Mickey's PhilharMagic）的奖励 FastPass。2003年2月17日，

cues.en: the one hundred millionth FastPass was distributed to the Dillon family of Atlanta, who were given a special golden Fastpass that allowed them Fastpass access to all attractions at the resort. Mike Dillon said, quote, things like this don't happen to the Dillons.
cues.zh: 第 一亿张 FastPass 发放给了来自亚特兰大的狄龙（Dillon）一家，他们获得了一张特别的金色 FastPass，凭此可畅玩度假村内的所有游乐设施。迈克·狄龙（Mike Dillon）说：“这种好事通常不会降临到狄龙家头上。”

cues.zh: 在 1871 年一个风雨交加的夜晚，

cues.zh: 杰贝迪亚·狄龙（Jebediah Dillon）偷偷溜上了一艘名为“玛吉女王号”（Queen Marge）的货船，这艘船即将驶入波涛汹涌的大西洋。驶向……哇，我觉得这里有点偏题了。不好意思。我刚才讲到哪儿了？到 2003 年，

cues.en: Fast Pass had grown significantly to 26 attractions at Walt Disney World. Five at Animal Kingdom, six at Disney MGM,
cues.zh: FastPass 已经大幅扩展到华特迪士尼世界的 26 个游乐设施。其中动物王国 5 个，迪士尼米高梅影城 6 个，

cues.en: five at Epcot, and 10 at Magic Kingdom. Disneyland Resort now had a total of 16 Fast Pass attractions,
cues.zh: 艾格柏特 5 个，神奇王国 10 个。迪士尼乐园度假区现在总共有 16 个 FastPass 游乐设施，

cues.en: nine at Disneyland and seven at California Adventure. The significant increase in FastPass attractions was due less to logistics and more to the monetary benefits of the system. During the late nineties and early two thousands, Paul Pressler, the chairman of Walt Disney Parks and Resorts, had instituted drastic cost cutting measures, slashing budgets across the board to increase profits.
cues.zh: 迪士尼乐园 9 个，加州冒险乐园 7 个。FastPass 游乐设施的大幅增加与其说是出于后勤考虑，不如说是为了系统的经济利益。在九十年代末和两千年代初，华特迪士尼公园和度假村董事长保罗·普雷斯勒（Paul Pressler）推行了激进的成本削减措施，全面缩减预算以增加利润。

cues.en: At the same time, Pressler, whose background was in retail, dramatically increased the amount of shopping and merchandise carts throughout the parks. Fastpass was a quick fix in many ways. Not only did the system promise to get guests out of the line and into gift shops, but Fastpass itself could be marketed far and wide as if it were a new attraction during a time when Disney didn't have anything else to promote. For a period of time in the mid two thousands, Fastpass was used as a perk for vacation packages, namely ones booked through triple a, which allowed guests access to what was referred to as enhanced Fastpass,
cues.zh: 与此同时，有着零售业背景的普雷斯勒大幅增加了园区内购物车和商品推车的数量。Fastpass在很多方面都是一个快速解决方案。这个系统不仅承诺让游客离开排队队伍、走进礼品店，而且Fastpass本身还能在迪士尼没有其他东西可宣传的时期，被当作一个新景点到处营销。在两千年代中期的一段时间里，Fastpass被用作度假套餐的福利，尤其是通过AAA预订的套餐，允许游客使用所谓的增强版Fastpass，

cues.en: which removed the two hour limit on guest tickets, allowing them to obtain as many FastPasses as available, with the only restriction being that they could not receive multiple passes for the same attraction until the first pass for that attraction had expired.
cues.zh: 它取消了游客门票上的两小时限制，让他们能获取尽可能多的Fastpass，唯一的限制是在某个景点的第一张Fastpass过期之前，不能重复获取该景点的多张通行证。

cues.en: With this, guests could enter Disneyland Park in the morning, obtain a Fastpass for every Fastpass attraction in the park, exit Disneyland Park, walk over to California Adventure, obtain a Fastpass for every Fastpass attraction at that park, and now, holding 16 Fastpasses,
cues.zh: 有了这个，游客可以早上进入迪士尼乐园，获取园区内每个Fastpass景点的Fastpass，离开迪士尼乐园，走到加州冒险乐园，获取那个园区每个Fastpass景点的Fastpass，而现在，手握16张Fastpass，

cues.en: have the best day ever, with the only downside being that they now have to experience seven attractions at a mid two thousands California adventure.
cues.zh: 度过史上最棒的一天，唯一的缺点是，他们现在得去体验两千年代中期加州冒险乐园的七个景点。

cues.en: The over implementation of FastPass did exactly what Stafford had predicted, and walkways at the parks were more congested than ever. This was especially noticeable at Disneyland, which is a much smaller park in comparison to the Magic Kingdom. The park was designed to have people waiting in line, but now, with most attractions using FastPass,
cues.zh: FastPass的过度实施完全如Stafford所预测，园区内的步道比以往更加拥挤。这在迪士尼乐园尤为明显，与魔法王国相比，它的面积小得多。园区设计本就是让人排队的，但现在大多数游乐设施都使用了FastPass，

cues.en: guests found themselves waiting through a sea of people, all waiting for their return time to arrive. Also, standby waits for high capacity attractions, such as Pirates of the Caribbean and Haunted Mansion, were noticeably increased with Fastpass.
cues.zh: 游客发现自己在一望无际的人海中等待，所有人都在等自己的预约时间到来。此外，高容量游乐设施的普通排队等待时间，如加勒比海盗和幽灵公馆，因FastPass而明显增加。

cues.en: In 2002, Paul Presler resigned to model for The Gap, where he would also serve as CEO. He was replaced by the chairman of Disneyland Paris, Jay Roussullo.
cues.zh: 2002年，Paul Presler辞职去为The Gap做模特，同时还将担任CEO。接替他的是巴黎迪士尼乐园的董事长Jay Roussullo。

cues.en: When Roussullo and other management took over, they reevaluated Disneyland's FastPass system, determining that the best solution was to begin removing FastPasses from certain attractions.
cues.zh: Roussullo和其他管理层接手后，重新评估了迪士尼乐园的FastPass系统，认定最佳方案是开始从某些游乐设施中移除FastPass。

cues.en: At Disneyland, Pirates of the Caribbean, Winnie the Pooh, and Star Tours had its fast pass kiosks removed, and Haunted Mansion's fast pass would only be utilized for Haunted Mansion Holiday. In California Adventure, It's Tough to Be a Bug and Muppet Vision had their fast passes removed as well. Eventually, the Haunted Mansion at the Magic Kingdom would have its FastPass removed. While FastPass worked well on some rides and did increase customer satisfaction significantly,
cues.zh: 在迪士尼乐园，加勒比海盗、小熊维尼和星际旅行拆除了FastPass取票机，幽灵公馆的FastPass只在幽灵公馆假日版中使用。在加州冒险乐园，虫虫危机和布偶秀的FastPass也被移除。最终，魔法王国的幽灵公馆也移除了FastPass。虽然FastPass在某些游乐设施上效果良好，并显著提升了顾客满意度，

cues.en: the over implementation within the first few years of its debut seemed to be clear proof that it was a bad idea to put FastPass everywhere.
cues.zh: 但推出头几年内的过度实施，似乎清楚地证明了到处都放FastPass是个坏主意。

cues.en: It is now September
cues.zh: 现在是九月

cues.en: It has been two years since Bob Iger became the CEO of Disney after an embattled Michael Eisner resigned. Fast Pass has just turned eight years old, and Jay Rizzulo is still heading the Parks division. It has also been recently announced that Disney was patenting a technology that would utilize a centralized computer system to manage FastPass tickets throughout Walt Disney World and Disneyland, allowing guests to obtain FastPasses from their mobile devices, which at the time looked like this.
cues.zh: Bob Iger在Michael Eisner黯然辞职后接任迪士尼CEO已有两年。Fast Pass刚刚满八岁，Jay Rizzulo仍在掌管乐园部门。最近还宣布，迪士尼正在申请一项技术专利，利用集中式计算机系统管理整个Walt Disney World和Disneyland的FastPass，让游客能从移动设备获取FastPass，当时的移动设备长这样。

cues.en: So most of the plans relied on sending text messages to guests.
cues.zh: 所以大部分方案都依赖给游客发短信。

cues.en: The patent application also stated that the new system could allow, quote, spending per guest at hotels
cues.zh: 专利申请还提到，新系统可以允许（引述）“按游客在酒店的消费额”

cues.en: to determine hierarchies of access to FastPass.
cues.zh: 来决定FastPass的获取优先级。

cues.en: Disney stated publicly that they had no plans to change FastPass at the moment, merely that they were monitoring how to take advantage of technological developments.
cues.zh: 迪士尼公开表示，他们目前没有计划改变FastPass，只是在研究如何利用技术发展。

cues.en: However, within the company, executives were formulating plans for a massive project in complete secrecy.
cues.zh: 然而在公司内部，高管们正在完全保密地筹划一个大型项目。

cues.en: Jay Roussullo and four other senior Disney Parks officials formed an exploratory committee to determine how the ongoing technological revolution could reinvent the guest experience.
cues.zh: Jay Roussullo和其他四位迪士尼乐园高级官员成立了一个探索委员会，研究正在进行的科技革命如何重塑游客体验。

cues.en: Like Walt Disney and Imagineers in the nineteen sixties, and like Bruce Laval in the nineteen nineties, Discussions once again centered on how to improve crowd control and wait times. The group was exploring multiple concepts when one member had an epiphany. While on a flight, VP of business development, John Padgett, was browsing through the in flight magazine Sky Mall, when he came across a magnetic wristband that promised to improve balance and reduce joint pain. This was of course a scam, but it gave Padgett an idea. What if Disney Park guests had their own wristband that contained technology that they could use around the park? It would be like a magic wristband,
cues.zh: 就像六十年代的Walt Disney和Imagineers，就像九十年代的Bruce Laval，讨论再次聚焦于如何改善人流控制和等待时间。团队探索了多个概念，直到一位成员灵光一现。在一次飞行中，业务发展副总裁John Padgett翻阅机上杂志Sky Mall时，看到一款磁性腕带，声称能改善平衡、减轻关节疼痛。这当然是骗局，但给了Padgett一个想法。如果迪士尼乐园游客有自己的腕带，内置技术可以在园内各处使用呢？就像一条魔法腕带，

cues.en: so naturally, they called it the Experience Band, or X Band for short. The team opened a testing space for X Band in the abandoned Body Wars attraction in the Wonders Of Life Pavilion at Epcot. After an ideation phase, Disney CEO Bob Iger was given a tour where the team explained their idea for the x band. Their proposal was to house an RFID tag inside the band that would allow guests to interact with touch points throughout the park. The X band could act as guest park tickets or their hotel room keys. They could even use it as a credit card. When Iger was shown the technology, he was impressed enough to give the project a proper budget. In 2008, development officially began on Disney Next Gen Experience, an initiative that promised to bring the guest experience into the modern age. This encompassed multiple strategies,
cues.zh: 于是他们自然地称之为Experience Band，简称X Band。团队在Epcot的Wonders Of Life展馆里废弃的Body Wars游乐设施中开辟了X Band的测试空间。经过头脑风暴阶段，迪士尼CEO Bob Iger来参观，团队向他介绍了X Band的想法。他们的方案是在腕带内嵌入RFID标签，让游客能与园内各处的触控点交互。X Band可以充当乐园门票或酒店房卡，甚至能当信用卡用。Iger看到这项技术后印象深刻，给项目批了正式预算。2008年，Disney Next Gen Experience正式启动开发，这项计划承诺将游客体验带入现代时代。它涵盖了多项策略，

cues.en: ranging from reinventing the way guests order food at the parks, to experimenting with different queue types to increase guest enjoyment while in line. Perhaps the most ambitious part of next gen was My Magic Plus, a complete overhaul of Walt Disney World's technological infrastructure and the introduction of a new website and mobile application.
cues.zh: 从彻底重构游客在园区点餐的方式，到尝试各种排队模式以提升排队时的游玩乐趣。而在 Next Gen 项目中最具野心的，或许要数 My Magic Plus——它对整个 Walt Disney World 的技术基础设施进行了彻底重构，并推出了全新的网站和移动应用。

cues.en: a magical app that will turn your Verizon mobile phone into a... Exclusive to Verizon. And it's super easy to use. Just touch characters.
cues.zh: “一款能把你的 Verizon 手机变成……的神奇 App。”Verizon 独占？“而且用起来超级简单，只要点击角色。”

cues.en: Disney and Verizon partnered on a new mobile app named Mobile Magic that allowed guests to see a map of the park, view show times, and play trivia for $9.99
cues.zh: Disney 和 Verizon 合作推出了一款名为 Mobile Magic 的新手机应用，游客可以查看乐园地图、演出时间，还能玩趣味问答，价格是 9.99 美元/

cues.en: every one hundred and eighty days? Jeez.
cues.zh: 每 180 天？天呐。

cues.en: impressive, the app allowed users to view wait times and fast pass return times from their phone, with real time information from the park's computer system. They could not book or view their FastPasses from the app, but this was still a powerful tool for the time, and it had a valuable feature. Guests could now bulk at an attraction's wait time from the other side of the park. Understanding the power the app had over guest decisions,
cues.zh: 厉害的是，用户能直接在手机上查看排队等待时间和 FastPass 返场时间，数据实时来自乐园的计算机系统。虽然无法在 App 里预订或查看自己的 FastPass，但这在当时依然非常强大，而且带来了一个极具价值的现象：游客人在乐园另一头，就能直接被某个项目的排队时长给劝退。在意识到这款 App 对游客决策的巨大引导力后，

cues.en: Disney began to inflate posted wait times to point guests in certain directions.
cues.zh: Disney 便开始故意虚标公示的等待时间，借此把客流引向特定区域。

cues.en: For instance, if there were too many people in Tomorrowland,
cues.zh: 比如，如果明日世界的人太多，

cues.en: Space Mountain's posted wait time might be adjusted to ninety minutes, despite the actual wait only being sixty, in order to dissuade guests from visiting the crowded area of the park. This also served the additional function of improving guest satisfaction,
cues.zh: 太空山的公示等待时间可能会被调整为九十分钟，尽管实际等待只有六十分钟，以此来劝退游客前往园区拥挤的区域。这还起到了提升游客满意度的额外作用，

cues.en: as actual waits were almost always shorter than posted waits, and it gave ride operators a buffer in the event of delays or downtime.
cues.zh: 因为实际等待几乎总是比公示时间短，而且这为游乐设施操作员在出现延误或停机时提供了缓冲。

cues.en: It is unclear when the strategy began, but it would become an integral part of My Magic Plus's crowd control features when the new app launched. In November 2009, two years into the development of Next Gen Experience,
cues.zh: 目前不清楚这一策略何时开始，但当新应用推出时，它将成为My Magic Plus人群控制功能中不可或缺的一部分。2009年11月，Next Gen Experience开发两年后，

cues.en: it was announced that Jay Roussullo would become the CFO of the Walt Disney Company, switching places with then CFO Tom Staggs, who would be taking Roussullo's position as the head of the Disney Parks. The switch was Iger's decision, and it was done to see which executive adjusted better to their new role. This was a way to help Iger determine his successor,
cues.zh: 宣布Jay Roussullo将出任华特迪士尼公司的CFO，与时任CFO Tom Staggs互换职位，Staggs将接任Roussullo的迪士尼乐园负责人职位。这一变动是Iger的决定，目的是看看哪位高管更能适应新角色。这是帮助Iger确定继任者的一种方式，

cues.en: as he planned to retire from the company in 2015.
cues.zh: 因为他计划在2015年从公司退休。

cues.en: Stags was inheriting the Next Gen program and My Magic Plus, and the pressure was immediately on for him to deliver on the team's plans, which had only become more ambitious. Not only did the Next Gen team want to reinvent park tickets and hotel keys, they wanted to completely overhaul Fast Pass as well. The new system would be titled X Pass, and it was a key feature of Next Gen's Guaranteed Experience initiative.
cues.zh: Staggs继承了Next Gen项目和My Magic Plus，压力立刻落到他身上，要求他兑现团队的计划，而这些计划只是变得更加雄心勃勃。Next Gen团队不仅想重新发明园区门票和酒店房卡，还想彻底改造Fast Pass。新系统将命名为X Pass，这是Next Gen“保证体验”计划的关键功能。

cues.en: The philosophy behind Guaranteed Experiences was to increase customer satisfaction and guest retention at the resort by removing unwanted variability in vacations.
cues.zh: Guaranteed Experiences 背后的理念，是通过消除度假中不必要的变数，来提高度假村的客户满意度和游客留存率。

cues.en: The program sought to ensure that guests would be able to eat at their favorite restaurants and ride their favorite rides during their trip. This is where X Pass came in. Guests would now be able to book multiple Fast Passes before they arrived at the park, and rather than using paper tickets, they would use their X Bands to enter the expedited queue. In late two thousand eleven, news broke on X Pass, mainly focusing on a rumor that Fast Pass would cost money. People took that great, but despite the uproar, the rumor turned out to not be true, at least not entirely.
cues.zh: 该项目旨在确保游客在旅行期间能在最喜欢的餐厅用餐，并乘坐最喜欢的游乐设施。X Pass 正是为此推出。游客现在可以在抵达乐园前预订多个 Fast Pass，并且不再使用纸质票，而是用 X Bands 进入快速通道队列。2011 年底，有关 X Pass 的消息传出，主要聚焦于一则传言：Fast Pass 将开始收费。人们对此反应强烈，但尽管舆论哗然，传言最终被证明不实——至少不完全属实。

cues.en: Fast Pass would still be available to everyone, but priority access would be given to those staying at a Walt Disney World Resort hotel. The plan was for guests to be able to book between two and four fast passes before they arrived. The specific number would be different for each park and would vary based on attendance. On the busiest days at Magic Kingdom, guests would only be allowed to book three fast passes, but on most days, they would be able to book four. However, at Epcot, which had significantly less attractions,
cues.zh: Fast Pass 仍将向所有人开放，但优先通道将提供给入住 Walt Disney World Resort 酒店的游客。按计划，游客可在抵达前预订 2 到 4 个 Fast Pass。具体数量因乐园而异，并会根据客流量变化。在 Magic Kingdom 最繁忙的日子，游客只能预订三个 Fast Pass，但大多数日子可以预订四个。然而，在景点明显更少的 Epcot，

cues.en: guests would only get to book two fast passes on busy days, while most days they would get to book three. The times for the reservations will be determined by guest preferences.
cues.zh: 客人在繁忙日只能预订两个 Fast Pass，而大多数日子可以预订三个。预订时间将根据游客偏好决定。

cues.en: Guests would input which attractions they wanted to ride, and an itinerary would be created with fast passes to optimize guest flow throughout the park. When paired with the rest of the next gen technology,
cues.zh: 游客会输入想玩哪些项目，系统会生成一份带 FastPass 的行程，用来优化园区内的游客流动。再配合下一代技术的其他部分，

cues.en: this had the potential to radically redesign crowd control. There was just one problem. Actually, were a thousand problems, but this was one of them.
cues.zh: 这就有可能彻底重新设计人群管控。但只有一个问题。其实有一千个问题，这只是其中之一。

cues.en: X Pass sought to offer multiple FastPasses to the majority of guests before their arrival. The problem was there were not enough FastPasses available at the resort's FastPass attractions to do this. In the original fast pass system, popular attractions would run out of fast passes for the day by noon or even before, and that was when people could only obtain one fast pass every two hours. Since fast pass already took up the majority of a ride's capacity,
cues.zh: X Pass 想在大多数游客到园前，向他们提供多个 FastPass。问题在于，度假区的 FastPass 项目没有足够的 FastPass 可用。在最初的 FastPass 系统中，热门项目到中午甚至更早就会发完当天的 FastPass，而当时人们每两小时只能领一个 FastPass。由于 FastPass 已经占用了游乐项目的大部分容量，

cues.en: and most rides at Walt Disney World were already operating at maximum capacity, it was not feasible to simply give out more FastPasses for these rides. When the industrial engineers ran the models for X Pass, it was apparent that there was not enough FastPass availability at the parks for the system to work. The engineers quickly realized that in order to offer multiple FastPasses to guests before they arrived, they would need to add FastPass to nearly every attraction at the resort. The total number of FastPass attractions at Walt Disney World would increase from 28 to 50. When the industrial engineers put the increased FastPass availability into the model, it still didn't work. Even with an additional 22 attractions,
cues.zh: 而 Walt Disney World 的大多数项目已经在满负荷运行，所以直接给这些项目发更多 FastPass 并不可行。工业工程师对 X Pass 跑模型时，明显看出园区没有足够的 FastPass 可用量让系统运转。工程师很快意识到，要在游客到园前提供多个 FastPass，就需要给度假区几乎所有项目都加上 FastPass。Walt Disney World 的 FastPass 项目总数会从 28 个增加到 50 个。当工业工程师把增加的 FastPass 可用量放进模型后，系统仍然行不通。即使多了 22 个项目，

cues.en: there were still numerous days throughout the year where FastPass availability would be gone before a significant amount of guests could book all of their passes. To solve this, it was suggested that fast pass be added not just to every attraction,
cues.zh: 一年中仍有很多天，在相当多游客订完所有 FastPass 之前，FastPass 就已经没了。为解决这个问题，有人建议不仅给每个项目加 FastPass，

cues.en: but also to things that were not typically considered attractions,
cues.zh: 也给那些通常不算游乐项目的东西加，

cues.en: such as meet and greets with characters.
cues.zh: 比如角色见面会。

cues.en: Apparently, this still wasn't enough, so it was suggested that guests could obtain fast passes to things that don't even have lines, such as firework shows or parades.
cues.zh: 显然，这依然不够，于是有人建议，游客甚至可以为那些根本不需要排队的项目（比如烟花秀或游行）获取快速通行证。

cues.en: Rather than skipping the line, special viewing areas would be created for these experiences and guests could book a fast pass to gain access to them. Finally, this increased,
cues.zh: 游客们将不再是跳过排队，而是为这些体验专门设立观赏区，游客可以预订快速通行证来进入这些区域。最后，这增加了一

cues.en: the amount of fast passes that could be offered, which helped support the idea to offer multiple fast passes to guests before they arrived. With the basic framework figured out, plans move forward on X Pass as Next Gen and My Magic Plus continue to develop. In February
cues.zh: 可提供的快速通行证数量，这有助于支持在游客抵达前向他们提供多张快速通行证的想法。随着基本框架的确定，随着 Next Gen 和 My Magic Plus 的持续开发，X Pass 的计划也在向前推进。2011
